idiom_name: struct of function pointers (jump table) + owned opaque implementation pointer
implementation_notes: C has no classes, so the whole structure is written out: the letter interface becomes a struct of function pointers (a jump or ops table, exactly as GObject puts method pointers into the class struct and the Linux VFS puts them into struct file_operations), the letter is an opaque struct behind a void pointer, and the envelope is a small struct holding the table pointer plus that pointer. What replaces nothing here - there is no compiler help at all: creation, cloning, swapping and destruction are explicit functions (create/clone/swap/destroy) and ownership lives in a comment or a naming convention. The classic form is the only form; when the set of realizations is closed, a tagged union plus a switch is simpler and lets the compiler see which cases exist, while a framework such as GObject supplies the same machinery if GLib is already in the stack.
pitfalls: The ops table belongs to the implementation, not to the object: keep one static const table per letter type, otherwise every envelope carries (and must free) its own copy of the function pointers.
Struct copy copies the pointer: the compiler generates no clone or destroy, so a copied envelope owns the same letter and a missing clone/free pair ends in a double free or a leak.
void * erases the letter's type, so the cast back must happen in exactly one place per letter; a mismatched cast is undefined behaviour rather than a compile error.
